content.title: Tennessee State AD ‘absolutely’ expects coach Nolan Smith to return after historic first season
content.text: Tennessee State coach Nolan Smith lifts a cut-down net in celebration after the Tigers won the OVC Championship and earned their first NCAA Tournament bid since 1994 on Saturday, March 7, 2026 against Morehead State. TSU ATHLETICS ST. LOUIS, Mo. – Tennessee State athletic director Mikki Allen was excited and expectant in the halls of Enterprise Center before the Tigers played Iowa State on Friday afternoon in the NCAA Tournament. Excited to have No. 15 TSU in March Madness for the first time in 32 years. And expectant “absolutely” that his first-year head coach would be back. In a transient era of college basketball, for both coaches and players, Nolan Smith’s stock soared in the months since he was hired as an assistant from the University of Memphis to lead Tennessee State. The national championship guard from Duke spoke freely on Friday about rebuilding for another season in Nashville following their 108-74 loss in the first round. “At the end of the day, Nolan’s expressed to me he wants to continue to build something special here,” Allen told Main Street Nashville. “He loves the geography of Nashville. The sky’s the limit for the Big Blue, and the last time I checked it’s always blue.” Tennessee State won 23 games this season under Smith, resetting its own Division I record, and claimed Ohio Valley Conference regular-season and tournament titles for the first time since 1994. He led a frantic defense that generated the seventh-most steals per game in Division I. Smith also coached the OVC Player of the Year in senior Aaron Nkrumah, who averaged 17.6 of their conference-leading 80.3 points. “I love building off of winning,” Smith said. “I’m obsessed with winning. … I say ‘winning’ probably a hundred times a day. So to be able to build off of this group, I’m excited to see what’s next and how we get another group that’s just like these guys that buy into winning, buying into being in March Madness consistently.” Allen said he wants Tennessee State to become a consistently competitive HBCU basketball program, similar to the likes of fellow NCAA Tournament team Howard and Norfolk State. To do that, Allen and Smith have discussed “an infusion of funds into our program, which our group is willing to do” to continually create high-level rosters and sustain and reward the coaching staff for their efforts. Some of this season could have been credited to former coach Brian “Penny” Collins who left most of his roster when he departed for a job with the Memphis Grizzlies in July. Smith kept the team together and added to it – namely in OVC Tournament MVP Dante Harris, the sixth-year Memphis carryover who also had stops at Georgetown and Virginia. Allen called Harris “probably one of the biggest recruits we’ve had.” “I feel like he’s gonna do great,” Harris said of Smith’s future. “I believe in him full force. You know, he’s a great coach and a great person.” In a lopsided loss to the Cyclones, Tennessee State’s 74 points were still the most scored by the program in a single tournament game. Nkrumah came within a 3-pointer of tying their individual scoring record in March Madness with 21 points. The Tigers battled early but fell away after 23 straight points in the first 10 minutes by Iowa State. “My staff and I, this is where we want to be,” at the NCAA Tournament, Smith said. “This is the expectation. When we wake up, we wake up every single day ready to win. So that’s what we’re gonna do, and these guys have now set the bar extremely high.” Mid-major college coaches have oftentimes pledged their allegiance to current programs at the end of a season, only to later bolt for a bigger program. New Kansas State coach Casey Alexander, for example, said he planned to be back at Belmont following his final game leading the Bruins in the Missouri Valley Conference Tournament. “Why wouldn’t you want to continue to do what you just did? Why wouldn’t you want to come back and repeat? We’ve set the table for that,” Smith said. “Now I’m going to go have some conversations with my athletic director and get this done so that we can run this back.”
